_note: HiveMind hackathon demo scenarios. All three themed incidents route to the ONE real, fixable bug (payment-service/config.yaml retry.timeout_seconds 1->5) — the theme lives in the alert narrative. service is ALWAYS 'checkout': it is the only value that simultaneously lights up Dynatrace Grail (service.name=checkout), the Elastic burst, and the BigQuery customer rows. Driven via scripts/demo.py.

scenarios.headline: World Cup final on-sale: checkout SLO breach under fan surge
scenarios.title: World Cup final ticket on-sale surge: checkout p99 latency doubled to 2x SLO after the payment-service v2.4.1 deploy — fans hitting Pay are timing out and being declined at the turnstile.
scenarios.aha: One alert during the on-sale spike — 90 seconds later HiveMind opened a merge request that fixes the exact config line and named the paying customers and revenue on the line, before an on-call human even opened a tab.
talk: This is THE live run on stage (Vertex is per-minute throttled, so only one fresh fire).
Watch the pills: Detective(Dynatrace) -> the parallel fan-out LogDiver(Elastic) / CodeArch(GitLab) / Liaison(BigQuery) -> Scribe(Atlas) -> Reviewer(Phoenix).
When CodeArch's MR link streams in, CLICK IT: a real gitlab.com MR, timeout_seconds 1->5, authored by @HiveMind-bot — not a screenshot.

scenarios.headline: Real-time card-payment deadline-exceeded: false declines on legitimate cardholders
scenarios.title: FRAUD/PAYMENTS SEV1: real-time card-payment authorization deadline exceeded — the fraud-decision path is aborting valid transactions, false declines spiking on legitimate cardholders and eroding trust.
scenarios.aha: A 'fraud' false-decline storm turned out to be a 1-second timeout aborting legitimate payments — HiveMind quantified the trust risk by name (4 Enterprise accounts ~ $20,600/mo) and opened the fix as a reviewable MR.
talk: Strongest theme for finance judges: a reliability bug masquerading as fraud-rejection, eroding trust.
Focus on CustomerLiaison's LIVE BigQuery output: ~7 customers on the payment path; the 4 Enterprise names CUST-011 $7,500, CUST-004 $5,800, CUST-001 $4,200, CUST-008 $3,100.
Lock the framing: '$21,646/mo at risk across the affected base' (annualized ~$259,752/yr) — pick one and stay consistent.

scenarios.headline: In-store POS tap-to-pay failing across mall tenants during a weekend campaign
scenarios.title: In-store POS checkout failing across mall tenants: card terminals timing out mid-sale at tap-to-pay during the weekend tenant campaign — registers retrying and aborting valid taps, shoppers abandoning at the till.
scenarios.aha: Same one-line alert from a mall's POS network — HiveMind autonomously walked logs -> metrics -> code -> customer impact and shipped a merge request the way a senior on-call engineer would, in under two minutes.
talk: Fired at sev2 (vs sev1) to show the severity field flowing end-to-end onto the channel + incident record.
Reinforces generalization: one engine, third industry, same converged fix.
Every run leaves a grounded postmortem in MongoDB Atlas with the MR link.

rigor_beat.theme: Meta / Rigor — it is real, not theater
rigor_beat.aha: An external evaluator grades the crew against a contract and catches it when it lies (it re-checks GitLab itself and FAILs a fabricated MR claim); and overnight the system rewrote its own review rubric and measurably got better — 6/10 to 10/10 catch rate — then promoted the winner automatically.
show: harness/runs/<id>/feedback.json — verdict=FAIL with 'required_final.mr_filed: claimed but no MR found in GitLab'.
Atlas harness_runs: the generator->evaluator loop self-corrects (FAIL->PASS) and gives up safely (FAILx4 -> ESCALATED to a human).
Atlas flywheel_runs: Reviewer rewrote its own rubric, old 6/10 -> new 10/10, promoted via the Phoenix 'production' tag (prompt version moved v1 -> v6).
honesty: Narrate only the 2 dated flywheel runs (the 3rd row is a plumbing stub).
